text:
Last night's Integration Debt Night at Kestrelmoor's Flatiron office was one of the more useful panels I've sat through this year. About 60 of us showed up to hear Priya Raman-Holt (VP Platform, Tallowbrook) and Marcus Feldane (founder, Quillary) on why integrations are where so much AI work stalls.

Takeaways:

1. Publish a spec instead of building one-offs. Tallowbrook maintains 140 partner integrations with just three engineers. Priya: "We stopped building connectors one by one and started publishing a spec. Partners build to it now."

2. Agent pilots fail at the seam, not the model. Marcus's team wires up data access before choosing a model.

3. The room agreed. When asked who had an agent pilot stall on data access, about 40 of 60 hands went up.

The best part was the disagreement. Priya thinks partners should own their connectors. Marcus thinks the platform has to own them or quality drifts. I left unsure who's right, and I suspect it depends on how much leverage you have over your partners.

For anyone running an agent pilot: have you sorted out data access yet, or are you still picking models?

Thanks to the Kestrelmoor team for hosting.
